reason: The text contains multiple human characters with clear agency. The Israelites act as a collective people - they flee (בָרַח הָעָם), lift their eyes to see the Egyptians approaching, express fear, cry out to the Lord, and speak to Moses with complaints and dialogue about their fate. Moses speaks and commands the people (וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל־ הָעָם), addressing their fears. Pharaoh and his officials deliberate ('What is this we have done?'), make decisions to pursue (וַיִּקַּח), and later attempt to flee when circumstances change. These are all regular human characters (not divine beings) demonstrating agency through speech, emotional response, decision-making, and action that drives the narrative.
